sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Westfield?
sections.html:
Westfield sellers deal with one fire department inspection, one county recording office and a quarterly tax bill, and the town does not ask for a resale certificate of occupancy. The pricing is the larger story: the median owner-occupied home here is valued at $953,400, which puts many sales close to the $1 million line where an extra state fee starts.

This page walks through the local numbers, the smoke and carbon monoxide inspection, deed recording in Union County and the town's tax calendar, so you can weigh a listing, a sale on your own and an as-is cash purchase with real figures in hand.

sections.h2: How does the Westfield housing market look on paper?
sections.html:
Westfield is a town of 32,595 people by the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate, up from 31,032 at the 2020 count. It covers 6.72 square miles of land, which works out to 4,615 people per square mile, and about 81 percent of homes are lived in by their owners.

Those figures describe a settled family suburb with few renters. Buyers who shop here are usually comparing Westfield with neighboring Cranford, Scotch Plains and Mountainside, so recent sales within a few blocks of your house tell you more than any town-wide median.

sections.h2: What do Westfield's history, downtown and schools mean for a sale?
sections.html:
Westfield was formed as a township on January 27, 1794, from part of Elizabeth Township, and it became a town in 1903. Its old village core dates to 1720, and the downtown still sits just north of the train station.

That downtown is managed by the Downtown Westfield Corporation through a special improvement district and holds more than 200 retail establishments, according to Wikipedia. Buyers who want to walk to dinner or the train pay attention to which side of the tracks a house is on, because the rail line divides the town into a North Side and a South Side.

The same split shapes the schools. Westfield Public Schools runs 10 schools with 5,979 students in 2023-24:

  • a central early childhood center for pre-kindergarten and kindergarten;
  • six neighborhood elementary schools for grades 1 to 5;
  • two intermediate schools, Roosevelt on the north side and Edison on the south side;
  • one high school, Westfield High School, for grades 9 to 12.

Parks add to the pull. Mindowaskin Park and Tamaques Park are in town, and the 450-acre Lenape Park is part of the Union County Rahway River Parkway.

sections.h2: Which roads and trains shape Westfield home values?
sections.html:
Commuting access is a main reason Westfield prices run so high. NJ Transit's Raritan Valley Line stops at Westfield station, with a one-seat ride to New York Penn Station during weekday off-peak hours and a faster run to Newark Penn on peak express trains.

Route 28 runs about two miles beside the tracks through the middle of town, and drivers reach the Garden State Parkway at Exits 135 and 137 or U.S. Route 22 on the northern edge. The NJ Transit 113 bus goes to the Port Authority Bus Terminal. Of the 108.63 miles of public road in town, 96.69 miles belong to the municipality, so street conditions are a local matter for most blocks.

When you describe your house to a buyer, give the walking time to the station and the nearest Parkway exit, since those two numbers move offers more than square footage does.

sections.h2: Does Westfield require a certificate of occupancy to sell my house?
sections.html:
No. The town's building department says Westfield does not require a certificate of occupancy or continued certificate of occupancy to sell a home. A Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Compliance is required instead.

Under the New Jersey Uniform Fire Safety Act, the owner of a one- or two-family dwelling must get that certificate from the Westfield Fire Department's Bureau of Fire Prevention before a sale or change of occupancy. Skipping it carries a $200 fine. The details sellers ask about most:

  • Inspections run on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 9 a.m. and noon, and no one calls ahead with a time.
  • The fee is $100 when the inspection is set more than 10 business days after payment, $125 for four to 10 business days and $150 for fewer than four.
  • An adult aged 18 or older must be home. The firefighters will not enter a vacant house on their own.
  • Ten-year sealed battery alarms meet the rule, and A/C powered detectors are accepted.
  • Open construction permits must be closed first, because the building department is notified.
  • A fire extinguisher is no longer required as of March 14, 2025.

The certificate is emailed if you give one address on the application, so list the closing attorney or agent who needs it. Even a house that a buyer plans to demolish needs the certificate.

sections.h2: Who records the deed and which state fees apply in Westfield?
sections.html:
Westfield is in Union County, so the deed is recorded by the Union County Clerk at 2 Broad Street in Elizabeth. The recording office is open Monday to Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with over-the-counter recording until 3:30 p.m. and no appointment needed. The clerk also keeps a satellite office at 300 North Avenue East in Westfield, though that location handles passports, notaries and business names rather than deeds.

The state charges the seller a realty transfer fee. For a sale above $350,000, the rate is $2.90 per $500 on the first $150,000, $4.25 on the next $50,000, $4.80 up to $550,000, then $5.30 and higher steps above that. Because Westfield's median value is $953,400, many sales here land in the $5.30 and $5.80 bands.

Sales above $1,000,000 also carry a Graduated Percent Fee on residential property: 1 percent of the total price up to $2,000,000, then 2 percent to $2,500,000, and higher percentages above that. A house priced at $1,050,000 therefore owes roughly $10,500 on top of the transfer fee, so ask your closing attorney to price it before you accept an offer near the line.

sections.h2: How do Westfield property taxes work when I sell?
sections.html:
The Westfield Tax Collector, at 425 E Broad Street, bills property taxes quarterly on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a 10-day grace period. When the tenth day lands on a weekend or holiday, the grace period runs to the next business day.

Late interest is 8 percent on the first $1,500 and 18 percent above that, counted back to the due date, and a returned check costs $20. Sewer fees are billed separately and are due each April 1. Because the town reminds new owners that a missing bill does not excuse the tax, ask the tax office for current balances on both taxes and sewer before closing, and have the closing agent divide the quarter between you and the buyer.

The office also helps residents apply for state relief programs, so a senior or veteran selling the house should confirm any deduction is cleared from the account.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell myself, or take a cash offer in Westfield?
sections.html:
Listing usually brings the highest price in Westfield, a cash purchase is faster and cleaner, and a sale on your own saves commission but puts every showing and contract task on you. Which one fits depends on the condition of the house and how soon you need to move.

  • List with an agent if the house is updated and you can wait through showings, a buyer's inspection and a mortgage approval.
  • Sell on your own if you know your block's recent sales and are comfortable with a real estate attorney handling the contract.
  • Take an as-is cash offer if you want to skip repairs and showings, are dealing with an inherited house or tenants, or need a closing date that fits your move.

Whichever route you pick, book the fire department inspection as soon as a closing date is in sight, since a Tuesday-or-Thursday slot can decide how fast you close. Compare written offers by what you net after the realty transfer fee, any Graduated Percent Fee, taxes and the mortgage payoff.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to sell a house in Westfield?
faqs.a: It depends on price, but the state realty transfer fee and the fire department inspection are the fixed items. The inspection runs $100 to $150, and the transfer fee follows the sale price, with the 1 percent Graduated Percent Fee added above $1,000,000. An agent's commission, if you list, comes on top of those.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection to sell my Westfield house?
faqs.a: Yes, a smoke and carbon monoxide alarm inspection from the Westfield Fire Department's Bureau of Fire Prevention is required before the sale. The building department says no certificate of occupancy is needed. Inspections are done on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 9 a.m. and noon.

faqs.q: When are Westfield property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a 10-day grace period. Sewer fees are due April 1. Interest runs at 8 percent on the first $1,500 of a delinquency and 18 percent above that.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Westfield house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. The inspection only checks alarms and carbon monoxide detectors, and open building permits must be closed before the certificate is issued. A buyer can take on cosmetic or structural repairs, which is how as-is sales work.

faqs.q: Where do I record a Westfield deed?
faqs.a: The Union County Clerk records it at 2 Broad Street in Elizabeth. The recording counter takes walk-ins with no appointment, and your closing attorney or title company normally handles the filing for you.
